items.title: Gunfire and explosions heard at Niger capital's airport
items.description: Niger has been fighting a militant Islamist insurgency for a decade and in January suspected jihadists attacked the same airport.

items.title: Cuba approves economic reforms amid US pressure
items.description: Cuba's Communist Party has signed off on a package of free market reforms. One member called the changes a response to "economic war," while the party said they were not a "deviation" from the socialist project.

items.title: Trump’s unfiltered commentary on Lebanon is leaving Israel with an impossible choice
items.description: Clearly tired of what Israel sees as an urgent fight, US president is making the contradictory claims that the war on Hezbollah is both not speedy enough and not careful enough The post Trump’s unfiltered commentary on Lebanon is leaving Israel with an impossible choice appeared first on The Times of Israel.

items.title: Ukraine hits Moscow refinery as Zelenskyy seeks Trump support to end war
items.description: Russia's Defence Ministry says air defences shot down 555 Ukrainian drones over several regions overnight.

items.title: Tehran and Washington sign interim peace deal to end US-Israeli war on Iran
items.description: President Donald Trump and his Iranian counterpart Masoud Pezeshkian on Wednesday signed an interim deal to end the US-Israeli war on Iran. items.title: Over 1,000 people killed during Gaza ceasefire, Palestinian authorities say
items.description: Israeli operations in the Gaza Strip have killed 1,005 Palestinians since a ceasefire was reached between Israel and the militant group Hamas last October, according to Gaza Health Ministry.

items.title: On Donbas front, warehouse manager aims to improve daily life for Ukrainian soldiers
items.description: In the Donbas, some combat zones have become too dangerous to deliver food, water and medicine to frontline infantry by road. A warehouse manager and amateur cook is doing everything he can to organize drone deliveries of varied food supplies and necessities.

items.title: 'It's Like Winning at Roulette': War Quotas Squeeze Russian Students Out of Free University Spots
items.description: Students say university admissions quotas for soldiers and their families are making state-funded places harder to win on merit alone.

items.title: Trump, 'ho avuto ottimi colloqui con Zelensky e con Putin'
items.description: 'Vorremmo vedere la fine di questa guerra'

items.title: G7 Pledges 'Unwavering Support' For Ukraine Amid Signs US Ready To Pressure Kremlin
items.description: Leaders of the Group of Seven (G7) nations have pledged their "unwavering support" for Ukraine and agreed to increase pressure on Russia through sanctions and weapons supplies to Kyiv amid signs Washington is turning its focus back toward ending Europe's deadliest conflict since World War II.

items.title: Resettlement remains out of reach for millions of refugees
items.description: As millions of people continue to flee their countries due to war or persecution, UNHCR, the UN refugee agency, called on Tuesday for an urgent expansion of refugee resettlement programmes, warning that available places continue to fall short of global needs.

items.title: Strike on Kyiv Lavra Is Like Bombing Notre-Dame, French FM Says
items.description: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot compared Russia’s strike on Kyiv’s historic Pechersk Lavra to bombing Notre-Dame or Saint-Denis, calling it part of Vladimir Putin’s colonial war against Ukraine. items.title: US-Iran ceasefire leaves Israelis feeling sidelined, their war aims unachieved
items.description: The U.S.-Iran ceasefire deal leaves many Israelis feeling vulnerable and abandoned by their most important ally. They voiced concern for Israel’s security, and some criticized Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for failing to achieve his war aims.
